newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister probed for illegal bugging.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister probed for illegal bugging.

text.p: A French magistrate placed a former minister and an ex-gendarme under judicial investigation on Tuesday over illegal phone-tapping by the late president Francois Mitterrand's anti-terrorist unit, justice sources said.

Michel Delebarre, who was chief aide to then prime minister Pierre Mauroy at the time of the scandal in the mid-1980s, and ex-captain Paul Barril, who belonged to the unit, were formally placed under investigation.
Magistrate Jean Paul Valat ordered Delebarre and three other unnamed persons believed to be ex-members of the unit probed as suspected accomplices to invasion of privacy, the sources said.
Delebarre, who served as labour and urban affairs minister in Socialist governments in the late 1980s and early 1990s, is now mayor of the northern port of Dunkerque.

Valat placed Barril under investigation on suspicion of holding illegally obtained computer files. The former paramilitary gendarmerie officer, who now runs a private security firm, is suspected of having kept and released some of the bugging unit's files.
Two former senior government officials, the former head and three members of the since disbanded anti-terrorist unit are already being investigated.

The Elysee presidential palace's anti-terrorist unit tapped the phones of dozens of politicians, lawyers and journalists without the required judicial permission. Barril himself became a target of the wiretaps after he left the unit.
